title: Radix-bucket tokenizer accelerator and hint-routing to reduce prefill overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Prefill-side preprocessing (tokenization + normalization + prefix dedupe) contributes a substantial fraction of total request latency for short-to-medium prompts and increases CPU cost on our serving fleet. Current path performs multiple passes over UTF‑8, branches heavily on character classes, and lacks a compact per-session hint index. This results in: higher p50/p95 prefill latency, wasted CPU cycles for repeated session prefixes, and backpressure into the decode scheduler when tokenization stalls.

Goals:
- Reduce prefill CPU time for common workloads by 30–40% (tokens/sec up to 1.4x).
- Cut p95 prefill latency by 30ms on typical 64–512 token prompts.
- Provide a low-overhead hint mechanism to avoid re-tokenizing common prefixes across requests in a session.
- Surface a small, stable metric to the kernel selector: prefill-length-distribution to allow attention kernel choices tuned for upstream tokenization characteristics.

Proposed solution overview:
1) Radix-bucket tokenizer accelerator: build a first-pass fast classifier that bins incoming byte ranges into 256 radix buckets; each bucket has a compact table of likely split points (ASCII common splits, byte sequences that start multibyte UTF‑8). For pure-ASCII hot paths this mostly avoids branchy UTF‑8 state machines. The accelerator is vector-friendly and intended to run as a single-pass pre-scan that emits hints instead of full subtokens when confident.

2) Hint-routing and per-session micro-index: maintain a tiny session-scoped cache (avg 128 entries, 16–64B per entry) keyed by content-hash of prefix windows. Entries map to token boundary offsets and normalization flags. This is designed as an optional fast-path lookup in the prefill lane; misses fall back to the full tokenizer. Entries are evicted by LRU and berkeley-style age thresholds to limit memory.

3) ASCII-normalization fastpath: many prompts are ASCII-heavy; add a specialized normalization kernel that performs lowercasing + whitespace squeeze + NFKC-lite in a single vectorized pass, avoiding general Unicode normalization costs for common inputs.

4) Speculative microtokenization for decode scheduler: when the accelerator emits confident hints, create provisional token batches and push them to the decode scheduler with a confidence bit. The scheduler can use confidence plus prefill-length-distribution to select lower-latency attention kernels or to speculatively allocate KV cache slots, improving downstream throughput. If later invalidated, rollback is cheap (we already maintain small change logs).

Integration points with runtime and kernel selection:
- Add an internal edge metric: prefill_length_histogram (buckets: 0–32,33–128,129–512,512+). Kernel selector will use this plus request confidence to weight kernel choices (e.g., use small-sequence-optimized attention kernels when prefill hints indicate short remaining decode lengths).
- Expose per-request hint flags in the runtime call path for tracing and rollout gating (internal-only header).

Success metrics and observability:
- Perf: tokens/sec improvement on our standard bench suite (chat-like prompts) >= 1.3x median, 1.4x best case.
- Latency: p50/p95 prefill latency reductions of 25–40% across representative datasets.
- Cost: CPU cycles per request down 30% on average for targeted workloads.
- Safety: fallback rate (accelerator miss or invalidation) under 10% for production traffic after 2-week canary.

Testing plan:
- Synthetic microbench harnesses (existing tokenization fuzzers) and corpus from customer telemetry (anonymized).
- A/B canary across edge cluster with full tracing enabled and automatic rollback on regressions (latency or fallback rate).
- Stress tests with long multibyte prompts to validate correctness and ensure no tokenization divergence.

Rollout plan:
- Internal feature flag gated rollout.
- Canary on non-critical LCU cluster 1 for 48h.
- Expand to 10% of production for 7d with dashboard checks.
- 100% rollout after quality gates.

comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Created initial ticket after spike showed 28% CPU reduction in microbench for ASCII-heavy corpus.
2026-03-03 - Liam Chen: Prototype radix pre-scan implemented; early numbers promising. Need to document fallback semantics with decode scheduler. Linked PR 1974.

2026-03-04 - Nora Kim (review): Reviewed design. Concern: session cache size per connection could amplify memory if not bounded. Recommend per-worker global budget + per-session soft limits. Action: add eviction policy details.
2026-03-06 - Liam Chen: Added LRU eviction and global worker quota to prototype. Bench updated: ASCII-only tests show 1.5x tokens/sec; mixed UTF-8 corpus shows 1.25x.

2026-03-08 - SRE: Need to ensure feature flag can be toggled remotely and that accelerometer doesn’t increase tail latencies under OOM. We added a circuit-breaker that bypasses accelerator when resident memory crosses threshold.

2026-03-10 - QA: Integration tests added for rollback correctness when speculative tokens are invalidated; no divergence observed in test suite (100k randomized prompts). Next: canary configuration and dashboard alerts.
